papers.title_en: Beyond Phenotypic Similarity: Relation Refinement and Selective Population Graph Learning for Multimodal Brain Disorder Diagnosis
papers.evidence: 用于多模态脑疾病诊断的图学习
papers.tldr: 群体图学习可借助受试者间信息共享辅助脑病诊断，但表型相似未必对应诊断一致，异质受试者需差异化表示更新。PopDRP以诊断标签校准属性亲和度，并用神经图修正融合功能连接与非影像表示；随后在选择性金字塔状态空间骨干中进行多分辨率图学习。ABIDE与ADHD-200十折交叉验证显示准确率和AUC优于基线，消融验证关系精炼与选择性分层骨干均有效。
papers.abstract_en: Population graph learning supports brain disorder diagnosis by sharing information across subjects. Its effectiveness, however, depends on whether the relationships guiding this exchange are relevant to diagnosis. Similarity in demographic or acquisition attributes does not necessarily indicate diagnostic agreement, and heterogeneous subjects may require different representation updates within the same population graph. We propose PopDRP, a framework that combines diagnosis-guided relation refinement with hierarchical selective state-space learning. Using only training labels, Contrastive Affinity Refinement calibrates attribute-based affinities according to diagnostic agreement. Neural Graph Rectification then refines these relationships using fused functional-connectivity and non-imaging representations, guided by graph reconstruction and dual-view alignment objectives. On the resulting graph, a Selective Pyramid State-Space backbone integrates input-dependent state updates, graph diffusion, and hierarchical pooling and unpooling to learn population representations at multiple resolutions. Together, these components connect the refinement of inter-subject relationships with selective representation learning over the population graph. Experiments on ABIDE and ADHD-200 under stratified ten-fold cross-validation show improved accuracy and AUC over the compared baselines. Ablation studies further support the contributions of relation refinement and the selective hierarchical backbone to classification performance.

papers.title_en: Convergent Performance, Divergent Mechanisms in LoRA-Adapted Vision Foundation Models for Brain MRI
papers.authors: Cecilia Diana-Albelda, Fiona Kekwick, Raghav Mehta, Aleksandra Kulbaka, Paul M. Matthews, Jesus Bescos, Álvaro García-Martín, Wenjia Bai, Bernhard Kainz
papers.evidence: 面向脑部MRI诊断的LoRA视觉基础模型
papers.tldr: LoRA适配视觉基础模型到医学影像常以下游指标选型，默认性能相近即机制等价。本文比较DINOv3、SigLIP2、MerMED-FM与BiomedCLIP四个ViT-B/16在脑肿瘤分割上的内部表征变化，并结合注意力差异、权重变化与激活修补分析。四者分割Dice相近（78–81%），但内部动态与跨任务迁移显著分化，且修改幅度不等于因果重要性。将LoRA限制在早中层可在保持分割的同时减轻分类退化，提供更参数高效且稳健的适配策略。
papers.abstract_en: Adapting Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) to medical imaging via LoRA has become standard practice, yet model selection is guided almost entirely by downstream task metrics, treating backbones with similar performance as interchangeable. We investigate whether equal performance implies equal internal representational shift. We analyse four ViT-B/16 backbones, DINOv3, SigLIP2, MerMED-FM, and BiomedCLIP, pre-trained with different objectives (self-distillation vs. contrastive vision-language) and on different data domains (natural vs. medical images). We adapt each to brain tumour segmentation and evaluate on six datasets covering both segmentation and Alzheimer's disease classification. Using attention divergence, weight-change analysis, and activation patching, we find that the four models converge to similar segmentation performance (mean Dice 78-81%) through markedly different internal dynamics, yet diverge in cross-task transfer: segmentation adaptation improves Alzheimer's disease classification for DINOv3 but degrades it for the other three backbones. We reveal a dissociation between modification magnitude and causal importance: the most heavily modified layers are not the causally relevant ones, with early-to-mid layers identified as sufficient for segmentation recovery. Restricting LoRA to these layers matches or approaches full-layer segmentation while reducing classification degradation in the three affected backbones, providing a mechanistically grounded strategy that is more parameter-efficient and more robust than standard full-layer adaptation.

papers.title_en: DGCM-SSFA: Dual-Granularity Cross-Modulation and Sparse Strip Frequency Attention for Efficient 3T-to-7T MRI Synthesis
papers.authors: Zhichun Fan, Zhiqiang Chen, Lanling Liu, Lingjun Liu, Zhonghua Xie
papers.evidence: 面向临床的神经影像MRI合成深度学习
papers.tldr: 从常规3T MRI合成高保真7T影像可规避超高场扫描成本，但现有深度学习方法常依赖超4500万参数或昂贵集成策略。DGCM-SSFA在U-Net Transformer主干中引入双粒度交叉调制模块与稀疏条带频率注意力，以多域注意力实现局部细节和全局频谱建模。模型仅约11M参数，在UNC和BNU的T1w/T2w 3T-to-7T任务上取得有竞争力的结构保真度，BNU T2w SSIM达0.8431。该工作为资源受限临床环境提供了轻量高效的跨场强合成方案。
papers.abstract_en: Synthesizing high-fidelity 7T MRI from routinely acquired 3T scans offers a practical pathway to enhanced neuroimaging without the prohibitive cost of ultra-high-field scanners. While existing deep learning approaches have achieved promising results, state-of-the-art methods typically rely on either large-scale architectures exceeding 45 million parameters or computationally intensive ensemble strategies, limiting their practicality in resource-constrained clinical environments. In this work, we propose a compact multi-domain attention framework, termed DGCM-SSFA, that achieves competitive synthesis quality with only 11M parameters. The proposed architecture integrates two complementary modules into a U-Net Transformer backbone. First, a Dual-Granularity Cross-Modulated Feature Modulator (DGCM) is embedded at multiple hierarchical levels to enhance local edge and texture details through Sobel-guided spatial attention and depthwise frequency-aware channel attention with cross-branch gating. Second, a Sparse Strip Frequency Attention (SSFA) module at the bottleneck captures global spatial context via strip-pooled attention with near-linear complexity, while simultaneously performing FFT-based spectral modulation in the frequency domain. These two modules operate synergistically with the backbone's native channel attention, forming a triple-granularity feature refinement pipeline. Extensive experiments on the UNC and BNU 3T-to-7T MRI datasets across T1w and T2w modalities demonstrate that DGCM-SSFA achieves strong structural fidelity, attaining an SSIM of 0.8431 on BNU T2w---approaching the best benchmark value of 0.8624---and 0.8100 on BNU T1w, while using substantially fewer parameters than Transformer-based alternatives such as ResViT (123.4M) and FS-RWKV (45.4M).
